ruling.reasoning:
The deviation is settled by the GPS record: 14.9 km driven against 10.7 km optimal, +4.2 km, over the 1 km tolerance, with one off-route segment 21:43–21:50 adding 3.70 km and reaching up to 1459 m off the optimal route [F1][F3][RD-1]. Nothing in the complete, timestamped chat names a rider-requested place or accepted destination change, so no kilometre is exempt under RD-3 [F7][F8][F10][RD-3].

The single decisive question is consent. At 21:40 the driver asked "mind if I go round via Telok Blangah Road?" [F7]; the rider replied "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway." [F8]. The segment began at 21:43 [F3], so the rider's message is pre-segment, but it is a refusal, not agreement: F3's ground is consent_after_or_none and the segment counts [F8][F3][RD-5]. Telok Blangah Road being one of the roads driven does not help the driver, because consent must be a rider's agreement and the record contains a refusal; the driver's post-trip statement "I asked the rider about the alternative road... I took it anyway" is a claim written after the trip and cannot supply consent [F11][RD-5][RD-3].

No traffic reason exists: Ayer Rajah Expressway ran at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h), no incident was recorded near the route, and the weather was fair, so the replaced stretch fails RD-4 and the "no traffic reason" row of RD-2 applies, which also records a driver violation [F12][F14][F15][RD-4][RD-2]. The refund is therefore the excess distance fare: (4.18 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare, platform fee and surge are not refunded, and no surge applied here (1.0×) [F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-0].

RD-6's add-on is not triggered: F17 records route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this is a first route/notification incident and the appropriate step is the RD-7 reminder and compliance log, not an account flag [F17][RD-6][RD-7]. The profiles (0 disputes for the rider, 2 upheld of 3 disputes for the driver) never decide the case [F16][F17][RD-6]. The amount is under $10, so under TH-1/TH-2 and DISP-001 the system rules finally, consistent with DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) [TH-1][TH-2].
